evidence: Start: AWS Service Impact section says Route 53 APIs were impaired beginning 7:30 AM PST, the moment the scaling activity set off the congestion. End: Issue Summary says every network device had recovered by 2:22 PM PST; console access returned then too. Regions: title and opening line place the disruption in Northern Virginia, US-EAST-1.
notes: The report gives no single time for the end of customer impact. The end is coded as the mitigation of the root cause (network devices fully recovered, 2:22 PM PST). Several services recovered later: EC2 launches 2:40 PM, STS 4:28 PM, API Gateway largely 4:37 PM, Connect 4:41 PM, Fargate 5:00 PM PST. EventBridge latency until 6:40 PM PST was backlog processing and is excluded. PST converted as UTC-8. Services counted (18): EC2, RDS, EMR, WorkSpaces, ELB, Route 53, Management Console, STS, Redshift, CloudWatch, VPC Endpoints (S3 and DynamoDB access through them), API Gateway, EventBridge, Fargate, ECS, EKS, Connect, Support Contact Center; the Service Health Dashboard and internal DNS and monitoring are not counted. The page text repeats the report body twice.

evidence: Start: AWS Service Impact section says the US-EAST-1 Management Console showed elevated errors from 11:48 AM PDT, one minute before Lambda errors began. End: Issue Summary says synchronous Lambda invocations fully recovered by 1:45 PM PDT and most affected services then recovered. Regions: title and summary confine the event to Northern Virginia, US-EAST-1.
notes: No publication date shown. The start is the Console's 11:48 AM PDT start, earlier than the 11:49 AM PDT Lambda start given in the summary. The end is 1:45 PM PDT, when Lambda and most dependent services recovered; the work between 1:45 PM and 3:37 PM PDT was asynchronous backlog processing and is excluded. Some services ended later: Console 2:02 PM, STS 2:10 PM, Sign-in 2:11 PM, Support Center 2:38 PM PDT. PDT converted as UTC-7. Services counted (8): Lambda, STS, AWS Sign-in, EventBridge, EKS, Management Console, Connect, Support Center. The page text repeats the report body twice.

evidence: Start: Summary of Impact says some users saw Graph API slowness and timeouts from 14:00 UTC on 16 December 2021. End: The same summary closes the impact window at 17:30 UTC. Regions: The report names only North America, with no Azure region.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (12/16/2021) is taken as its publication date. Scope is unclear because the report names only North America and no Azure region; the mitigation moved traffic to other healthy North American regions, also unnamed. The entry is marked Mitigated with a preliminary root cause. Service counted (1): Microsoft Graph API.

evidence: Start: Summary of Impact says SQL Database connection errors in West Europe began at 07:31 UTC on 16 Feb 2022. End: The same summary ends the impact window at 15:31 UTC. Regions: Title and summary name West Europe as the only affected region.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (02/16/2022) is taken as its publication date. The fault was one router of eight in a network tier; no zone is named. Services counted (2): SQL Database, App Service.

evidence: Start: Summary of Impact says B2C sign-in and sign-up errors began at 09:13 UTC on March 16, 2022. End: The same summary ends the impact window at 10:22 UTC. Regions: Root Cause refers only to the affected region without naming it.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (03/16/2022) is taken as its publication date. Scope is unclear because the report mentions an affected region but never names it. Service counted (1): Azure Active Directory B2C.

evidence: Start: Summary of Impact says service management errors in East US 2 began at 12:25 UTC on 08 Apr 2022. End: The same summary ends the impact window at 14:40 UTC on 09 Apr 2022. Regions: Title and summary name East US 2 only.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (04/08/2022) is taken as its publication date. The root cause mentions a zonal failure of an Allocator service, but no zone is named, and the impact was to service management across the region, so scope is regional. Services counted (9): Azure portal, Virtual Machines, Virtual Machine Scale Sets, Data Factory, Databricks, Synapse, Backup, Site Recovery, Virtual Desktop; the Compute Resource Provider Gateway and Allocator are internal components and are not counted.

evidence: Start: What happened says ACS authentication and API failures began at 18:13 UTC on 12 Aug 2022. End: The impact window closes at 03:30 UTC on 13 Aug 2022, when the hotfix finished rolling out. Regions: The title says Multiple Regions without naming any of them.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (08/12/2022) is taken as its publication date. Scope is unclear because the title says Multiple Regions and names none; the report calls ACS globally distributed but does not say the impact was global. Service counted (1): Azure Communication Services; its affected features (SMS, Chat, Email, Voice and Video, Phone Number Management, Teams-ACS Interop) are counted as one product. The resource provider and Cosmos DB backend are not counted as impaired customer services.

evidence: Start: What happened says packet loss on West Europe traffic began at 02:34 UTC on 16 June 2023. End: How did we respond says loss rates returned to normal at 07:25 UTC, which closes the stated window. Regions: The impact centred on West Europe, and Azure Databricks was also hit in North Europe through a control plane dependency.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (06/16/2023) is taken as its publication date. Coded multi_region because two regions are named with impact; North Europe was affected only for Azure Databricks. Traffic between availability zones inside West Europe was also affected, but no zone is named. The network was substantially recovered by 06:12 UTC; the end is taken as 07:25 UTC, the close of the stated impact window. No separate start is given for North Europe. Services counted (38): 33 named Azure services plus Microsoft 365, Intune, Purview, Sentinel and Power Platform.

evidence: Start: What happened says managed identity token and management failures began at 00:55 UTC on 12 July 2024. End: The same window ends at 06:28 UTC, which How did we respond gives as full mitigation. Regions: The failures were in Australia East, with every zone there affected.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (07/12/2024) is taken as its publication date. Australia Southeast is mentioned as the failover pair whose requests also failed for Australia East identities; the report does not describe customer impact in Australia Southeast, so it is not coded as a region. Services counted (7): Managed Identities for Azure resources, Virtual Machines, Virtual Machine Scale Sets, Service Fabric, Azure Stack HCI, Databricks, Kubernetes Service.

evidence: Start: What happened and the response timeline put the start of customer impact at 14:47 EDT on 27 September 2024. End: The timeline says the impact was mitigated at 16:25 EDT by reverting the misconfiguration. Regions: Says ARM in all Azure US Government regions was hit, naming US Gov Arizona, Texas and Virginia.
notes: The date at the top of the entry (09/27/2024) is taken as its publication date. This report gives times in EDT, not UTC; they are converted as UTC-4. Coded global because the report says the global account change impacted ARM in all regions; this refers to the Azure US Government cloud, and the three regions it names are listed. The end is the close of the stated impact window, which the timeline calls customer impact mitigated. Services counted (23): Azure Resource Manager plus 22 named downstream services; the misconfigured Cosmos DB account is not counted as an impaired customer service.
